newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SECURITIES REGISTRY CHARGES NEW OFF-MKT FEE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SECURITIES REGISTRY CHARGES NEW OFF-MKT FEE.

text.p: The Czech Central Securities Registry (SCP) said on Wednesday that it would begin assessing a fee equal to 0.5 percent of the turnover of each trade, on securities transactions performed off organised markets.
In a statement, SCP director Jiri Sedlacek, said the new fee would take effect on August 1.
The new fee comes amid a total overhaul of charges assessed by the state-controlled SCP.

Czech government officials and market participants have takes steps recently to encourage more trading to take place on the country's two organised markets -- the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) and the retail-oriented RM-System.
The PSE has imposed a ban on its members trading shares of companies listed on its main and parallel markets outside of the two organised markets from August 1.

A large majority of turnover in Czech securities has been concentrated in direct trades which have been simply registered at the SCP. Analysts say that this practice has drained the market of liquidity and transparency.
